_readme: Graded prices from pricecharting.com, keyed by card name and number.
A SNAPSHOT, NOT A FEED. Written by scripts/sync-pricecharting.mjs when it
is run by hand. Every record carries the url it came from and the file
carries the date, and the pages print both, because these do not refresh
overnight the way the raw TCGdex prices do.
RAW PRICES STILL COME FROM TCGDEX. `ungraded` here is kept only so the
graded figures can be compared against the raw price PriceCharting itself
saw. Where the two sources disagree the site quotes TCGdex for raw,
because that is the number every other page uses.
SCOPED TO CARDS WE PULLED. Do not run this over the whole card index: a
product page is about 1MB and 4,481 of them is roughly 4.4GB of somebody
else's bandwidth for data that would appear on a handful of pages.
`number` IS WHAT WE SEARCHED WITH, `matched` IS WHAT CAME BACK. They are
not two copies of one fact. An empty `number` means data/hits.json named
no number for that card, so the lookup went out on the name alone and
nothing has confirmed the printing.
DO NOT BACKFILL AN EMPTY `number` FROM `matched`. It looks like free data
and it is not. Checked against the set checklists on 2026-08-14, 4 of the
12 numberless records had landed on a different printing of the right
card: Dawn #129 where ours is #118, Mega Gardevoir ex #178 where ours is
#159, Mega Venusaur ex #177 where ours is #003, Cetitan ex #210 where
ours is #065. Copying those in would state that we pulled the secret
rare, and it would erase the empty string that is the only marker of
which records were never verified. build-hall.mjs reads `matched`, not
`number`, precisely so it can catch these, and it drops the price when
the two disagree.
